exhibition.d: a collection of things (goods or works of art etc.) for public display

exhibition game.d: a game whose outcome is not recorded in the season's standing

exhausted.d: drained of energy or effectiveness; extremely tired

exhibition hall.d: a large hall for holding exhibitions

exhaust fan.d: a fan that moves air out of an enclosure

exhaust system.d: system consisting of the parts of an engine through which burned gases or steam are discharged

exhibition area.d: a large hall for holding exhibitions

exhibition season.d: the time before the regular games begin when football or baseball teams play practice games

exhaust hood.d: metal covering leading to a vent that exhausts smoke or fumes

exhaust valve.d: a valve through which burned gases from a cylinder escape into the exhaust manifold

exhaust fumes.d: gases ejected from an engine as waste products

exhaust pipe.d: a pipe through which burned gases travel from the exhaust manifold to the muffler

exhaust manifold.d: a manifold that receives exhaust gases from the cylinders and conducts them to the exhaust pipe

exhaustion.d: serious weakening and loss of energy

exhibitionist.d: someone who deliberately behaves in such a way as to attract attention

exhibitionism.d: the perverse act of exposing and attracting attention to your own genitals

exhibitor.d: someone who organizes an exhibit for others to see

exhibitioner.d: someone who organizes an exhibit for others to see

exhibitionistic.d: compulsively attracting attention to yourself especially by public exposure or exaggerated behavior

exhilaration.d: the feeling of lively and cheerful joy

exhume.d: dig up for reburial or for medical investigation; of dead bodies

exhumation.d: the act of digging something out of the ground (especially a corpse) where it has been buried

exhalation.d: the act of expelling air from the lungs

exhort.d: spur on or encourage especially by cheers and shouts

exhortation.d: the act of exhorting; an earnest attempt at persuasion
